gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Noto Sans Marchen has small letters that stand nearly as tall as capitals. Edo SZ answers with cast-iron stature and one constant stroke width, so a larger size suits it while the sans-serif text stays modest.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mayan-num: Noto Sans Mayan Numerals reads tall-bodied and contemporary, its gaping c obvious at any size, while Edo SZ draws its heading like smooth wire. Over many lines the sans keeps its upright, open rhythm.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-medefaidr: Edo SZ holds every stem and curve at a single width, with a lowercase that has cast-iron stature. Noto Sans Medefaidrin rises high in its lowercase and never pools ink where curves turn, so a long passage moves along easily.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-meetei-ma: Noto Sans Meetei Mayek has large lowercase eyes and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle, which feels thoroughly modern. Shrink Edo SZ and its pencil-like, never-thickening lines lose their cast-iron stature.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mende-kik: Daylight shows through every curve of Noto Sans Mende Kikakui, and its lowercase stands tall against the capitals. Noto Sans Mende Kikakui stays clean across a long stretch, while Edo SZ keeps rounds and stems in one weight.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Noto Sans Meroitic is approachable, with see-through c openings and lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals. And Edo SZ matches that fullness, its tails and terminals as thick as the stems.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-modi: Edo SZ has a drafting-pen outline quality, one constant nib width from cast-iron lowercase to tail. Noto Sans Modi brings daylight inside every curve, and that openness is what the two share.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mono: Noto Sans Mono spaces its letters generously so they never bump, and its tall lowercase makes words look sturdy. But Edo SZ is the one with presence, its strokes free of thick and thin.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-mro: Noto Sans Mro makes words look dense and tall through the middle, with wide entrances into each letter. And Edo SZ presses its strokes in like twine on a flat surface, giving the pair real texture.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-multani: Noto Sans Multani has a lofty x-height and an e with a wide terminal gap. Edo SZ, with zero stroke contrast throughout, gives that sans-serif an unusually sturdy partner.
